notes: Check batch at 551e3ab with the uncommitted Readability rewrite plus one sentence added since evals/sweeps/2026-10-31-check: four skill runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), no opus, so opus is unavailable in per_rule. All four have rc 0 and a model_id matching their tier, and each result.json records skill_hash 24d7ee6e..., which equals the evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of the current idiomatic-elixir/ folder; every transcript contains the added sentence ("A `fn` is the one head this does not cover"). The transcripts' Read calls are SKILL.md and the run's orders.ex only (haiku-1 also wrote a Decimal stand-in at /tmp/orders_stub/stub.exs, outside its run folder), so reads is SKILL.md for all four and Expected reads (none) is met. In the scratch folder all four pass mix format --check-formatted and run against the stand-in Decimal of earlier graders: totals, last-order dates (a -02:00 order at 23:30 falls on the next UTC day) and empty results for [] are correct in all four. Haiku-1 and sonnet-2 return a named {:error, ...} for a missing key, a bad amount, an unknown status, a bad date and a non-string amount; haiku-2 returns {:error, :invalid_row} for a missing key and {:error, {:unknown_status, "lost"}}; sonnet-1 returns {:error, {:invalid_order, row}} for every bad row; haiku-2 and sonnet-1 pass a non-string amount to Decimal.parse/1 unchecked, which raises FunctionClauseError (no listed rule covers it, as in earlier grades).

Rules changed since d04061d and graded against the current text: the with rule, the do: rule, the pipeline rule, the captures rule, the Enum/Map table (two new rows, neither shape present), the renamed `->` rule and the two new rules. The with rule is decided by "One step is a `with` only when its body cannot fail and there is no `else`" (build/1 in all four) and by "A body that is one call whose `{:ok, value}` or `{:error, reason}` goes out as the function's own result ... is a tail call, not a second step, and the one-step `with` stays" (haiku-1 37-39, sonnet-1 87-89, sonnet-2 77-79). Two judgment calls under it: haiku-2's case Enum.find(...) with error -> error (lines 54-65) is held clean because the sentence "A `case` whose error clause is `{:error, _reason} = error -> error` is the same pass-through spelled out over four lines; write it as the `with`" names a fallible call's result, and this case is on a search result whose success shape is nil; sonnet-1's three-step with with a one-clause else (line 113: :error -> {:error, {:invalid_order, row}}) is held clean under the unchanged sentence "A large `else` block that maps errors back to steps is hard to follow", as the 2026-10-22 rate-limiter baseline-haiku-1 grade held a one-clause else that wraps every error alike, though its step helpers return bare :error rather than {:error, reason}. The do: rule adds no violation: no run has a one-line if, a fn or a call-carrying capture in a do: body, haiku-2's one for is do ... end, and the mixed functions (haiku-1 parse_rows/2, haiku-2 parse_order/1, sonnet-1 parse_orders/2 and parse_order/1, sonnet-2 parse_orders/2) set block clauses apart with blank lines. The pipeline rule finds no one-line pipeline in any run.

Captures rule, decided by "A `fn` that binds names takes the room its names earn: the body goes on the line after the `->`, and `end` closes it on a line of its own". Every fn written: haiku-1 lines 95-97 fn {customer_id, customer_orders} ->, 120-122 fn {currency, amounts} ->, 127-129 fn {customer_id, summary} ->, 130-132 fn {_customer_id, count} ->, 133-135 fn {customer_id, count} ->, all with the body on the next line and end on its own line; haiku-2 lines 121-123 fn {customer_id, customer_orders} ->, 146-148 fn {currency, currency_orders} ->, 157-159 fn customer ->, all multi-line; sonnet-1 lines 142-144 fn {customer_id, customer_orders} -> and 160-162 fn {currency, amounts} -> multi-line, line 169 fn {customer_id, count} -> {-count, customer_id} end on one line; sonnet-2 lines 146-148 and 160-162 multi-line, line 169 the same one-line sort_by fn. So 2 of 4 runs violate (sonnet-1, sonnet-2), against 3 of 4 in 2026-10-31-check: Haiku went from 1 of 2 to 0 of 2 (both Haiku runs here write every fn over several lines, haiku-1 including its sort_by fn at 133-135), and both Sonnet runs again write the one-line Enum.sort_by(fn {customer_id, count} -> {-count, customer_id} end) after frequencies_by. Captures with two placeholders: haiku-2 line 152 &Decimal.add(&1.amount, &2), in order and each once, which the rule allows.

One expression per line, and tabular clauses (clean in all four). Constructs: the parse_status/1 do: tables (haiku-1 86-89, haiku-2 107-110, sonnet-1 134-137, sonnet-2 138-141) and sonnet-2's completed?/1 (173-174), decided by "Parallel clauses may stay compact ... when they form a table"; the one-line do: heads (haiku-1 34; haiku-2 90; sonnet-1 84, 117; sonnet-2 72, 74) and one-line -> clauses (haiku-1 65-67, 73-75, 81-82; haiku-2 94-96, 102-103; sonnet-1 113, 121-123, 129-130), each a selection and one tuple or value, decided by "A line reads in one pass when it holds a selection and the one expression that selection produces"; the long single-line bodies {:ok, %{customers: summarize_customers(orders), top_customers: top_customers(orders)}} (sonnet-1 80, sonnet-2 68) and sonnet-2's %{totals: totals_per_currency(orders), last_order_on: DateTime.to_date(latest.placed_at)} (153), decided by "Count expressions, not calls or brackets". The sonnet runs' one-line sort_by fn (line 169) is no longer a judgment under this rule: the added sentence "A `fn` is the one head this does not cover: when it binds names, its body goes on the next line whatever that body is, under the capture rule below" sends it to the captures rule, where it is graded.

Name a step instead of wrapping an expression (clean in all four). Constructs: the bindings order (haiku-1 51, haiku-2 78), orders = for ... (haiku-2 56-59), last_order_at and latest_placed_at (haiku-1 105, haiku-2 130), latest (sonnet-1 148, sonnet-2 152) and results (haiku-2 52, used twice), decided by "A binding earns its place when it names a recognizable thing or a stage of the computation", so none "only renames a value used once"; the sonnet runs' formatter-wrapped {:ok, %Order{...}} (sonnet-1 104-111, sonnet-2 91-98), held clean as in 2026-10-31-check because it is a tag around a struct literal laid out one field per line, with no distinct computational steps to name. No run wraps a nested computation.

Inline `->` clauses that read at a glance; otherwise put each body on its own line (violated in sonnet-1 and sonnet-2, against haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 in 2026-10-31-check). Both violations are the one-line sort_by fn at line 169, decided by "A `fn` passed as an argument follows the capture rule: when it binds names, its body goes on the line after the `->`." Clean constructs: haiku-1's string_field/2 (64-68, three clauses, a guarded valid row and two error rows), parse_amount/1 (72-76) and parse_placed_at/1 (80-83), haiku-2's parse_amount/1 (93-97) and parse_datetime/1 (101-104), and sonnet-1's parse_amount/1 (120-124), parse_placed_at/1 (128-131) and with ... else (112-114), each body one expression beside its pattern, held clean by "or when each body is one expression simple enough to take in together with its pattern", every clause under 70 characters after the indentation (longest 66, haiku-1 line 65, a pattern with a two-condition guard); haiku-2's case on Enum.find (54-65) and sonnet-2's cases (103-112, 116-125, 129-135), every body on its own line with blank lines between clauses, as "when one clause breaks, every clause of that `case` does" requires.

Unchanged rules (atoms, lists, dates, money, Naming, processes) are graded to the 2026-10-23 standard. Other rules: haiku-1 gives build/1 a @doc without ## Examples (the documentation rule, as in earlier sweeps); haiku-1 reports the last order as a DateTime and haiku-2 keeps customers with no completed orders in top_customers, which no rule covers. Haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 have doctests; no case or with is nested inside another in any run, and no other violation was found.
